key_insight: The paper proposes preserving a model’s behavior rather than protecting its parameters, allowing a single shared prompt to learn new tasks while retaining older knowledge. The supplied abstract is truncated, so the exact anchoring mechanism and results cannot be verified.
problem_solved: Updating one shared prompt can overwrite knowledge of previously learned classes. The challenge is to prevent this forgetting without replaying old training examples or adding task-specific prompts.
method: Keep a pre-trained vision transformer frozen and adapt it through a small set of learnable prompt tokens.
Share one prompt across all tasks rather than maintaining separate task-specific prompts.
Anchor behavior while updating the shared prompt for new tasks; the supplied excerpt does not specify the anchoring objective.
impact: This approach targets parameter-efficient continual learning without storing old examples or growing a collection of prompts. Its practical effectiveness and performance trade-offs are not available in the supplied excerpt.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: a frozen vision transformer paired with one trainable shared prompt.
Task timeline: successive tasks update the same prompt, with no replay buffer.
Conceptual comparison: protecting parameters versus preserving model behavior.

paper_title: Anchor Behavior, Not Parameters: Rehearsal-Free Continual Learning with a Single Shared Prompt
paper_authors: Duy-Cuong Bui, Trung-Anh Dang, Vincent Nguyen, Duc V. Le, Ngoc-Son Vu
